title: 5 Simple Gadgets to Speed Up Garlic Prep for Holiday Cooking

html:
When you’re prepping a holiday feast, garlic is a must‑have flavor booster, but peeling and mincing it can eat up precious time. Luckily, a few smart garlic prep gadgets can cut the effort in half, letting you focus on the turkey, pies, and family. Below are five simple tools that streamline garlic prep for holiday cooking, plus a few bonus items that keep the whole kitchen running smoothly.

1. Sturdy Garlic Press – The Workhorse for Quick Mince

The classic garlic press is the undisputed champion of fast garlic prep. A solid stainless‑steel press with silicone-coated pistons crushes cloves instantly, turning a whole bulb into a fine paste in seconds. The best models also feature a built‑in cleaning brush, so you can scrape out residual bits without disassembling the whole tool. For holiday cooking, where you might need a tablespoon or more of minced garlic for stuffing, sauces, and marinades, a good press saves both time and effort.

2. Herb Scissors – Mince Garlic and Herbs in One Snip

If you like to combine garlic with fresh herbs for a bright, aromatic finish, herb scissors are a game‑changer. Five‑blade scissors chop garlic, cilantro, chives, and basil simultaneously, delivering uniform pieces that meld perfectly into vinaigrettes or herb rubs. The built‑in cleaning comb makes it easy to remove stuck fibers, and the ergonomic handles reduce hand fatigue when you’re working through dozens of cloves.

3. Onion Holder & Slicing Guide – Stable Cutting for Consistent Pieces

While primarily designed for onions, the Onion Holder & Slicing Guide also excels with garlic bulbs. The stainless‑steel prongs grip the garlic firmly, keeping it steady while you slice. This eliminates the classic “slip‑and‑cut” hazard and produces even slices that can be roasted whole or added to braising liquids. The same tool doubles as a meat tenderizer, making it a versatile addition to any holiday prep station.

4. Mandoline Slicer – Ultra‑Thin Garlic Slices for Quick Roasting

When you need garlic to caramelize quickly, thin slices are essential. A mandoline slicer with an adjustable blade lets you set the thickness to a near‑paper‑thin level, so garlic cooks evenly in a flash. Hand guards protect fingers, and the quick‑slide design means you can process a whole bulb in under a minute. Pair the mandoline with a sturdy cutting board and you have a fast, safe method for creating garlic ribbons for salads, soups, and holiday side dishes.

5. Wooden Spurtle & Sourdough Starter Stirrer Set – Scrape, Mix, and Clean Garlic‑Infused Liquids

After crushing garlic in a sauce or broth, you’ll often need to scrape the bottom of the pot to release stuck bits. The Wooden Spurtle & Sourdough Starter Stirrer Set includes a skinny spurtle spatula that slides easily under stubborn pieces, and a Danish‑style dough stick that works great for stirring thick marinades. Both are gentle on cookware and help keep your garlic‑infused sauces smooth without extra scrubbing.

Bonus Kitchen Essentials for a Smooth Holiday Meal

While you’re gearing up for holiday cooking, consider adding a few complementary gadgets that keep the rest of the kitchen humming:

  • Instant-Read Meat Thermometer – Ensure turkey and roasts hit the perfect internal temperature without guesswork.
  • Silicone Baking Mats – Replace parchment on cookie sheets, making cleanup a breeze after baking garlic‑bread or herb crackers.
  • Jar & Bottle Opener – Open stubborn wine bottles or pickle jars with ease, especially when you’re juggling multiple dishes.

These tools don’t directly handle garlic, but they free up your hands and time, letting you focus on flavor.

How to Use Your Garlic Gadgets Efficiently

1. Prep the cloves: Break the garlic head into individual cloves. Use the garlic press for the majority of your minced garlic; reserve a few whole cloves for roasting.
2. Slice or chop: For recipes that call for thin slices (like garlic confit), run the cloves through the mandoline set to the thinnest setting. Use the herb scissors when you need a quick mince that includes herbs.
3. Secure and cut: Place the garlic in the Onion Holder & Slicing Guide, then slice uniformly. This step is especially handy for stuffing a turkey with garlic‑infused aromatics.
4. Scrape and stir: After cooking, use the spurtle to scrape the bottom of the pot and the stirrer to blend the garlic into sauces or gravies.
5. Clean quickly: Most presses and scissors have built‑in cleaning tools. Rinse the mandoline under running water and wipe the spurtle with a damp cloth to keep everything ready for the next batch.

Why These Gadgets Matter for Holiday Cooking

Holiday meals often involve multiple dishes, each demanding precise flavor balance. Garlic is a cornerstone ingredient, and any shortcut that maintains quality is worth the investment. Using a garlic press or herb scissors reduces prep time by up to 50%, allowing you to attend to other critical steps like timing the turkey or monitoring the pumpkin pie. Moreover, tools like the Onion Holder & Slicing Guide improve safety—an essential factor when you’re juggling hot pans, busy kids, and festive drinks.

FAQ

Do I need a separate tool for peeled versus unpeeled garlic?

No. A good garlic press works on both peeled and unpeeled cloves. Just trim the ends, and the press will crush the clove cleanly.

Can I use the herb scissors for other small veggies?

Absolutely. The five blades handle scallions, chives, and even thinly sliced carrots, making them a versatile addition to any holiday prep routine.

Is the mandoline safe for beginners?

Yes, as long as you use the hand guard and keep your fingers away from the blade. Many models also include a safety lock for added confidence.
